read.sections.0.text.back: An invention is a new tool, machine or way of doing something. About 5,500 years ago, people in Mesopotamia used the wheel to shape pots from clay. Later, people attached wheels to carts to carry heavy loads of grain and goods, so that farming and trading became easier. Printing is another example. About 1,000 years ago in China, a man named Bi Sheng made small blocks of clay, each with one written sign. Printers could move the blocks around to print new pages. Later, printers in Korea used metal blocks. In the 1400s, Johannes Gutenberg made a printing machine in Germany. Books became cheaper, so more people could read and share ideas.
read.sections.0.text.source: An invention is a new tool, machine or way of doing something. About 5,500 years ago, people in Mesopotamia used wheels to shape clay pots. Later, people put wheels on carts to carry heavy loads of grain and goods, which made farming and trade easier. Printing is another example. About 1,000 years ago in China, a man named Bi Sheng made small clay blocks, each with one written sign. Printers could move the blocks around to print new pages. Later, printers in Korea used metal blocks. In the 1400s, Johannes Gutenberg built a printing press in Germany. Books became cheaper, so more people could read and share ideas.

read.sections.0.simpler.back: An invention is a new tool or way of doing something. Very long ago, people in the area that is now Iraq used the wheel to make pots. Then people attached wheels to carts. Carts could carry heavy things. Printing is also an invention. In China, Bi Sheng made small blocks of clay. Each block had one sign. Then people in Korea made metal blocks. Then Gutenberg made a printing machine in Germany. The price of books became cheaper. So more people could read.
read.sections.0.simpler.note: Review: 'di daerah yang sekarang Irak' is a little elliptical; the standard text says 'yang sekarang menjadi Irak'. Consider 'yang sekarang bernama Irak'.
read.sections.0.simpler.source: An invention is a new tool or way to do something. Long ago, people in what is now Iraq used wheels to make pots. Later, people put wheels on carts to carry heavy loads. Printing is another invention. In China, Bi Sheng made small clay blocks, each with one sign. Later, people in Korea made metal blocks. Then Gutenberg made a printing press in Germany. Books cost less, so more people could read.

read.sections.1.text.note: 'even without a bank' rendered as 'bahkan tanpa rekening bank' (without a bank account), which I think is the intended meaning.
read.sections.1.text.back: Some newer inventions spread very fast. With mobile phones, people can call, send messages and look for information. In Kenya, a service that started in 2007 let people send small amounts of money by phone, even without a bank account. Solar lamps are another example. In the daytime, sunlight charges a battery inside the lamp. At night, the lamp lights up without an electric cable. In the past many families used kerosene lamps, which were smoky and whose oil had to be bought again and again. With solar lamps, people can cook, read or study after dark. But an invention only helps people who have access to that invention.
read.sections.1.text.source: Some newer inventions spread very quickly. Mobile phones let people call, send messages and find information. In Kenya, a service that started in 2007 lets people send small amounts of money by phone, even without a bank. Solar lamps are another example. During the day, sunlight charges a battery inside the lamp. At night, the lamp gives light without any power lines. Many families once used lamps that burned kerosene, which made smoke and had to be bought again and again. With a solar lamp, people can cook, read or study after dark. But an invention only helps people who have access to it.

read.sections.1.simpler.back: Some new inventions spread fast. With mobile phones, people can call, send messages and look for news. In Kenya, people can send money by phone. Solar lamps are charged by sunlight. At night, the lamp lights up. Old lamps used oil and were smoky. With solar lamps, people can read at night. But inventions only help if people have access to that invention.
read.sections.1.simpler.source: Some new inventions spread fast. With a mobile phone, people can call, send messages and find news. In Kenya, people can send money by phone. A solar lamp charges in the sun and gives light at night. Old lamps burned oil and made smoke. With a solar lamp, people can read after dark. But an invention only helps if people have access to it.

read.sections.2.text.back: Look at the bicycle trial in Riverstone. Cycling to the market takes 12 minutes, not 30, so Amara saves 18 minutes. That is a real benefit. But the price of a bicycle is 80 tokens, and Hana cannot pay it. Repairs also need spare parts and skills. The steps on the shortcut are a barrier, because riders must carry their bicycle up the stairs. Some people cannot ride a bicycle, or do not want to. Inventions can also cause problems that nobody planned. Cars make travel faster, but also make the air dirty. So, when you study an invention, ask who can use it, who decides, and what could help more people.

write.example.back: This trial shows that cycling saves Amara 18 minutes on the shortcut to the market. One of the benefits is that she has more time for other work. However, one of the barriers is cost. The price of a bicycle is 80 tokens, so Hana cannot get one. The steps on the shortcut are also a barrier. Before giving out more bicycles, I will test the longer road without steps. I will also ask whether people can share bicycles. This will help more people because more people can use a bicycle safely.
write.example.source: The trial shows that cycling saves Amara 18 minutes on the direct route to the market. One benefit is that she has more time for other work. However, one barrier is the cost. A bicycle costs 80 tokens, so Hana cannot get one. The steps on the direct route are also a barrier. Before giving out more bicycles, I would test the longer route with no steps. I would also ask if people could share bicycles. This would help more people because more of them could use one safely.

watch.summary.back: This video tells the story of the cotton-seed separating machine (cotton gin), a machine invented in the United States in 1793. Cotton plants produce soft white fibre, which is used to make cloth. Before this machine, workers had to pull the seeds from the cotton by hand, and this work was very slow. The cotton gin could do it much faster. Now one worker could do the work of about 10 people. Growing cotton started to make much more money, and the cotton business grew fast. But the machine also brought terrible consequences that nobody planned. Cotton plantations grew larger, and plantation owners forced far more enslaved people to work there. Slavery lasted longer. This video shows that one invention can bring wealth and great suffering at the same time.
watch.summary.source: This video tells the story of the cotton gin, a machine invented in the United States in 1793. Cotton plants grow soft white fibre, which is used to make cloth. Before the machine, workers had to pull the seeds out of the cotton by hand, and this was very slow. The cotton gin did the job much faster. One worker could now do the work of about 10. Growing cotton began to earn much more money, and the cotton business grew fast. But the machine also had a terrible effect that no one planned. Cotton farms grew, and farm owners forced many more enslaved people to work on them. Slavery lasted longer. The video shows that one invention can bring both wealth and great harm.
